newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh strike disrupts transport, business.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh strike disrupts transport, business.

text.p: Bangladesh's nearly one million factory and transport workers walked off the job on Wednesday to protest the government's privatisation policy and to demand higher wages, government and union officials said.
"The country's economic life has almost collapsed due to the workers' strike," said one government official in southeastern Chittagong Port city.
Workers barricaded roads and train lines, disrupting transport across the country, communication ministry officials said.
Bangladesh's umbrella body of workers' federations, Sramik Karmachari Oikya Parishad (SKOP), called the 24-hour national strike after talks with the government to avoid a work stoppage failed.
Goods at Chittagong port were not moving, port officials said. "But only 30 percent of cargo handling has been affected," one official said.
Many business houses across the country were closed and the Dhaka Stock Exchange operated with fewer traders.
"We rejected a request to withdraw our strike...since we have not been assured that our demands would be considered," Kamrul Hassan, a SKOP leader told Reuters.
He said at least 5,000 mills and factories had been closed since 1991 and thousands of workers at state-owned companies had been sacked.
The government had also recently called for bids to sell 13 public state companies under its privatisation programme, he added.
